p0.original: 第一章 让爱融入生活
p0.en: Chapter 1: Bringing Love into Our Lives

p2.original: 我相信，人天生热爱生命，乐于互助。可是，究竟是什么，使我们难以体会到心中的爱，以致互相伤害？又是什么，让有些人即使在充满敌意的环境中，也能心存爱意？
p2.en: I believe that people naturally love life and enjoy helping one another. Yet what makes us lose touch with the love in our hearts and hurt each other? And what enables some people to remain loving even in a hostile environment?

p3.original: 这样的思考始于童年。大约是1943年的夏季，我家搬到了密歇根州的底特律。到达后的第二个星期，公园中一起暴力事件引发了种族冲突，接下来几天有40多人遇害。我家处于冲突的中心地带，整整三天，我们都紧闭家门，不敢出去。
p3.en: I began asking these questions as a child. Around the summer of 1943, my family moved to Detroit, Michigan. During our second week there, a violent incident in a park sparked racial conflict. More than forty people were killed over the following days. Our home was in the middle of the conflict, and for three full days we kept our doors shut, afraid to go outside.

p4.original: 冲突结束后，学校复课了。我发现，和肤色一样，名字也可能招来危险。老师点名时，有两个男孩瞪着我，嘘声说：“你是Kike吗？”我从未听过这个词，不知道它是某些人对犹太人的蔑称。放学后，他们在路上拦住我，把我摔在地上，拳打脚踢。
p4.en: When the conflict ended, school resumed. I discovered that a name, like skin color, could put someone in danger. When the teacher called my name, two boys stared at me and hissed, ‘Are you a kike?’ I had never heard the word and did not know that some people used it as a slur against Jewish people. After school, they stopped me on the way home, threw me to the ground, and punched and kicked me.

p5.original: 从此，上述两个问题就一直困扰着我。是什么赋予我们力量，使我们在最恶劣的情况下，也能关爱生命？给我启发的是像艾提·海勒申（Etty Hillesum）那样的人。即使被关押在德国人惨无人道的集中营，她依然一片柔情。在日记中，她写道：
p5.en: Those two questions have stayed with me ever since. What gives us the strength to care for life even in the harshest circumstances? People such as Etty Hillesum inspired me. Even while imprisoned in an inhumane German concentration camp, she remained compassionate. In her diary, she wrote:

p6.original: “我不会轻易害怕。那不是我勇敢，而是我知道，他们也是人，我必须用心理解他们的行为。今天早上，那个性情粗暴的年轻盖世太保冲我吼叫，我没有生气，而是关心他。我想问：‘你的童年很不开心吗？女友抛弃你了吗？’他看起来愁眉苦脸、躁动不安、阴沉而又虚弱。我当时就想帮助他。他那么痛苦，一旦为所欲为，是多么危险！”
p6.en: "I won't be easily afraid. It's not that I'm brave, but I know that they're human, and I have to understand what they're doing. This morning, the young Gestapo, who was rude, yelled at me, and I was not angry, but concerned about him. I'd like to ask, "Did you have a bad childhood?" Did your girlfriend abandon you? 'He looks sad, restless, dark and weak. I was trying to help him. He's in so much pain, how dangerous it is to do whatever he wants!

p7.original: ——艾提·海勒申：日记一则我认识到语言及表达方式的巨大影响。也许我们并不认为自己的谈话方式是“暴力”的，但我们的语言确实常常引发自己和他人的痛苦。后来，我发现了一种沟通方式，依照它来谈话和聆听，能使我们情意相通，乐于互助。我称之为“非暴力沟通”。这里借用甘地曾用过的“非暴力”一词，来指暴力消退后，自然流露的爱。在一些地区，这种沟通方式被称为“爱的语言”；在本书中，“NVC”指非暴力沟通或爱的语言。
p7.en: — Ayti Helsen: I recognize the great impact of language and expression in a diary. Perhaps we do not think that our way of talking is “violence”, but it is true that our language often causes suffering to ourselves and others. Later, I found a way to communicate, to talk and listen to it, and to be able to make us feel the same and to be happy to help. I call it “Nonviolent Communication”. The term “non-violent”, once used by Gandhi, is used here to refer to the love that emerges when violence recedes. In some regions, this mode of communication is referred to as the “language of love”; For the purposes of this book, “NVC” means a language of Nonviolent Communication or love.

p9.original: 非暴力沟通的基础是一些沟通方式——即使在逆境中，它们也能使人乐于互助。非暴力沟通没有任何新的主张，它所吸纳的内容，都有悠久的历史。它的目的正是提醒我们借助已有的知识，让爱融入生活。
p9.en: Nonviolent Communication is based on a number of means of communication — they can make people happy to help each other even in adversity. There is no new idea of Nonviolent Communication, and it incorporates a long history. It is precisely a reminder that we can build on the knowledge that exists to integrate love into life.

p10.original: 非暴力沟通指导我们转变谈话和聆听的方式。我们不再条件反射式地反应，而是去明了自己的观察、感受和愿望，有意识地使用语言。我们既诚实、清晰地表达自己，又尊重与倾听他人。这样，在每一次互动中，我们都能聆听到自己和他人心灵深处的呼声。同时，它还促使我们仔细观察，发现正影响我们的行为和事件，并提出明确的请求。它的方式虽然简明，但能带来根本性的变化。
p10.en: Nonviolent Communication guides us in changing the way we talk and listen. Instead of being conditioned to reflect, we have become aware of our observations, feelings and aspirations and have consciously used our language. We express ourselves honestly and clearly, while respecting and listening to others. In this way, in each interaction, we can hear the voices of our own and others' hearts and minds. At the same time, it prompts us to look closely at the behaviour and events that are affecting us and to make a clear request. Its approach, while simple, can bring about fundamental changes.

p11.original: 听到批评时，我们一般会申辩、退缩或反击。然而，一旦专注于彼此的观察、感受及需要，而不反驳他人，我们便能发现内心的柔情，对自己和他人产生全新的体会。这将最大限度地避免暴力。通过强调倾听——倾听自己及他人，非暴力沟通培育彼此的尊重、关注与爱，使人乐于互助。
p11.en: When criticism is heard, we usually argue, retreat or counter-attack. However, once we focus on each other's observations, feelings and needs without refuting others, we find the tenderness of our hearts and give ourselves and others a fresh sense of it. This would maximize the avoidance of violence. By emphasizing listening — listening to oneself and others — Nonviolent Communication fosters respect, concern and love among one another and makes one happy to help one another.

p12.original: 虽然我称非暴力沟通为“沟通方式”，但它不只是沟通方式。它更是一种持续不断的提醒，使我们专注于更可能满足我们人生追求的方向。
p12.en: Although I call Nonviolent Communication a “communication”, it is not just a communication. It is more a constant reminder that we are focusing on the direction that is more likely to meet the direction that we seek in our lives.

p13.original: 有个故事讲述一个男人在街灯下趴着寻找东西。一位路过的警察问他找什么。那个有些醉意的男人回答道：“找车钥匙。”警官就问：“是在这丢的吗？”他说：“哦，在公园丢的。”看到警察很困惑，他急忙解释：“这里的光线要亮得多。”
p13.en: There's a story of a man lying down in the streetlight looking for something. A passing policeman asked him what he was looking for. The drunk man replied, "Look for the car keys. The police officer said, "Did you lose it here?" He said, "Oh, it was in the park. “The light here is much brighter.

p14.original: 让爱融入生活是我毕生的追求——我与他人情意相通、乐于互助。可是，由于主流文化的影响，我迷失了方向。于是，我想借非暴力沟通来看清并专注于自己的人生选择。
p14.en: I've always wanted to be part of my life — I've been with others and I've been happy to help. But I lost my way because of the influence of mainstream culture. So I want to look at and focus on my life choices through Nonviolent Communication.

p15.original: 我所说的“乐于互助”，在下面这首抒情诗中得到了很好的表达：
p15.en: The words “favouring to help one another” are well expressed in the following love poem:

p17.original: 是我得到的最好的礼物，
p17.en: It's the best gift I've ever had.

p18.en: When you know I'm with you

p20.en: You know, I'm not giving you anything.

p22.en: It's because I want to live.

p31.en: I am grateful for your assistance.

p35.original: 当我们真诚助人时，我们丰富他人生命的愿望得到了满足。我们的行为，是出于由衷的喜悦。这样的给予让施者和受者同时受益。由于施者的给予既不是出于恐惧、内疚或羞愧，也不是为了得到什么；受者获得馈赠，却不会有心理负担。与此同时，施者会因自己行为的价值更加欣赏自己。
p35.en: Our desire to enrich the lives of others is met when we truly help. We acted out of sincere pleasure. Such a grant benefits both the giver and the recipient. (b) because the giving is neither out of fear, guilt or shame, nor for what; Recipients receive gifts without having a psychological burden. At the same time, practitioners would appreciate themselves more for the value of their actions.

p36.original: 非暴力沟通的使用，并不需要沟通的对象熟悉非暴力沟通，或对我们心存善意。如果我们遵循非暴力沟通的原则，乐于互助，并表明那是唯一的动机，那么，他人也会加入我们，最终形成良好的互动。我并不是说这种局面总会很快出现。但我确信，只要信守非暴力沟通的原则和方法，友爱之花必将在你我心中怒放。
p36.en: The use of Nonviolent Communication does not require familiarity with Nonviolent Communication or goodwill on our part. If we follow the principle of Nonviolent Communication, are willing to help each other and show that that is the only motive, then others will join us and eventually have good interaction. I am not saying that this will always happen soon. But I am sure that the flower of love will be in your heart and mine as long as we adhere to the principles and methods of Nonviolent Communication.

p38.original: 为了彼此能乐于互助，我们专注于四个方面——非暴力沟通模式的四个要素。
p38.en: In order to be happy to help one another, we have focused on four aspects — the four elements of a model of Nonviolent Communication.

p39.original: 首先，留意发生的事情。我们此刻观察到什么？不管是否喜欢，只是说出人们所做的事情。要点是，清楚地表达观察结果，而不判断或评估。接着，表达感受，例如受伤、害怕、喜悦、开心、气愤等等。然后，说出哪些需要导致那样的感受。一旦用非暴力沟通诚实地表达自己，前三个要素就会得到体现。
p39.en: First, keep an eye on what's happening. What do we see right now? Whether you like it or not, just say what people do. The main point is that the observations are clearly expressed without judgement or assessment. Then, it's like feeling, like getting hurt, being scared, being happy, being happy, being angry. And then, say what needs to lead to that feeling. The first three elements are reflected when they are expressed in an honest manner through Nonviolent Communication.

p40.original: 举例来说，一位母亲可能对她处于青春期的儿子说：“费利克斯，看到咖啡桌下的两只脏袜子和电视机旁的三只，我不太高兴，因为我看重整洁。”
p40.en: For example, a mother may say to her adolescent son: “Felix, I'm not happy to see two dirty socks under the coffee table and three by the TV, because I think it's clean.

p41.original: 接着，她立即提出非暴力沟通的第四个要素——具体的请求：“你是否愿意将袜子拿到房间或放进洗衣机？”这一要素明确告知他人，我们期待他采取何种行动，来满足我们。
p41.en: She then immediately submitted the fourth element of Nonviolent Communication — a specific request: “Will you take the socks to your room or put them in the washing machine? This element clearly informs others of what we expect him to do to meet us.

p42.original: 这样，这位母亲就清楚地说出非暴力沟通的四个要素。借助这四个要素诚实地表达自己，是非暴力沟通的一个方面。非暴力沟通的另一方面是借助它们关切地倾听。我们首先通过体会他人此刻的观察、感受和需要，与他们建立联系，然后聆听他们的请求，来发现做什么可以帮助他们。
p42.en: In this way, the mother made clear the four elements of Nonviolent Communication. The honest expression of one's identity through these four elements is an aspect of Nonviolent Communication. Another aspect of Nonviolent Communication is the use of them to listen with concern. We first find out what can be done to help others by understanding their observations, feelings and needs at the moment, by connecting them and then listening to their requests.

p43.original: 保持对这两方面的关注，并帮助他人也这么做，双方便可持续互动，直至情意相通：我此刻的观察、感受和需要是什么；为了改善生活，我的请求是什么；你此刻的观察、感受和需要是什么；为了改善生活，你的请求是什么……
p43.en: Maintaining attention to both aspects and helping others to do the same will allow both sides to interact on a sustainable basis until they understand each other: what I see, feel and need at this point; What is my request to improve life? What are your observations, your feelings and your needs at this moment? To improve your life, what is your request?

p44.original: 使用非暴力沟通时，表达自己或倾听他人，都是好的开端。但需要牢记的是，非暴力沟通不是固定的公式，它可以适应不同的情况，并根据个人风格及文化环境做出调整。为了叙述的方便，我将非暴力沟通称为“沟通方式”，但有时语言是多余的。非暴力沟通的精髓在于对其四个要素的觉察，而不在于使用什么字眼进行交流。
p44.en: The use of Nonviolent Communication, expressing oneself or listening to others, is a good start. It is important to bear in mind, however, that Nonviolent Communication is not a fixed formula that can be adapted to different circumstances and adapted to individual styles and cultural contexts. For ease of description, I refer to Nonviolent Communication as a “communication”, but sometimes language is superfluous. The essence of Nonviolent Communication lies in the perception of its four elements, not in the use of words for communication.

p46.original: 无论自我对话、与人交谈，还是小组讨论，非暴力沟通都能使我们心存爱意。因此，它适用于各个层面的交流和各种环境：
p46.en: Nonviolent Communication, whether self-dialogues, people-to-people conversations or panel discussions, can make us feel loved. It therefore applies to all levels of communication and the environment:

p53.original: 任何性质的争论和冲突
p53.en: Any kind of controversy and conflict

p54.original: 有些人用非暴力沟通增进与伴侣的感情：
p54.en: Some people use Nonviolent Communication to promote relationships with their partners:

p55.original: “当我运用非暴力沟通与他交流，我不再觉得受伤，也没有退缩，而能倾听和领会他的情感。我发现，这个与我结婚28年的男人，内心原来那样痛苦！在我参加［非暴力沟通］研讨班前的那个周末，他甚至提出了离婚。长话短说，幸亏非暴力沟通挽救了我们的婚姻，否则，今天我们不可能一起来到这里……我试着体会他的感受，说出我的需要，听取不中听的回答。他来这里不是为了讨我欢心，我来也不是为了他的幸福。我们学着成长、接纳和爱，只有这样才能各得所愿。”
p55.en: “When I use Nonviolent Communication to communicate with him, I do not feel injured, I do not retreat, but I can listen to and appreciate his feelings. I found out that the man I married for 28 years was so painful inside! He even filed for divorce that weekend before I attended the workshop on [Nonviolent Communication]. To be brief, it is fortunate that Nonviolent Communication saved our marriage, otherwise we would not have been here together today... I try to feel his feelings, speak my needs, hear my unheard answers. He didn't come here to please me, and I didn't come here for his happiness. We learn to grow, embrace and love, so that we can all be equal.

p57.original: 还有人用非暴力沟通改进工作。一位教师写道：
p57.en: Nonviolent Communication has also been used to improve efforts. A teacher wrote:

p58.original: “在特殊教育的课程中，我使用非暴力沟通大约已有一年。有些学生具有表达困难、学习障碍和行为问题，但也能运用非暴力沟通。比如，有位学生在教室中吐痰、咒骂、尖叫，并用铅笔戳走近他课桌的同学。我提醒他：‘请换一种方式表达。使用长颈鹿语言。’（在一些研讨班中，长颈鹿形状的木偶，被用作解释非暴力沟通的教具）他立即站起来，看着本想指责的同学，平静地说：‘你靠我这么近，我都要生气了！离我的桌子远点好吗？’另一个学生也许会说：‘没问题！我忘了你不喜欢这样。’
p58.en: “In the special education curriculum, I have been using Nonviolent Communication for about a year. Some students have difficulties in expressing themselves, learning disabilities and behavioural problems, but are also able to use Nonviolent Communication. For example, a student spitting, swearing, screaming in a classroom and poking a pencil at his class table. I remind him: "Please speak in another way. Use giraffe language. He immediately stood up and looked at his classmates who wanted to blame him, and said, "You're so close to me, I'm so angry!" Stay away from my desk, will you? The other student might say, "No problem! I forgot you didn't like it. # I'm not sure #

p59.original: 我开始思考为什么我会有挫折感。我想知道，除了和谐与秩序，我还需要什么。我投入大量时间备课，可为了管理课堂，无法好好讲课。这也影响了其他学生的学习。当他再次发作时，我开始告诉他：‘我很看重学习。请认真听讲好吗？’也许，一天中要提醒他一百次，但他一般都会重新开始认真听课。”
p59.en: I began to wonder why I would be frustrated. I want to know what else I need besides harmony and order. I spent a lot of time preparing classes, but I couldn't do it properly to manage the class. This also affects the learning of other students. And when he did it again, I began to tell him, "I'm learning a lot. Will you listen carefully? 'Maybe he'll be reminded a hundred times a day, but he'll normally start listening.

p60.original: ——伊利诺伊州芝加哥市的一位教师

p62.original: “在行医时，我经常使用非暴力沟通。一些病人问我是不是心理学家，因为医生通常并不关心他们的生活方式以及对疾病的态度。非暴力沟通帮助我敏锐地觉察他们的需要，了解特定的时刻他们需要听些什么。这对改善与血友病人和艾滋病人的关系特别有用——此类医患关系常常受到强烈愤怒和痛苦的冲击。在过去的五年，有位患艾滋病的妇女接受了我的治疗。最近，她提到，我努力帮她寻找生活的乐趣，是她得到的最大帮助。非暴力沟通功不可没！在过去，一旦得知病人患了致命的疾病，我就心灰意冷，难以真诚地鼓励他们拥抱生活。通过运用非暴力沟通，我开拓了视野，找到了新的沟通方式。它与医疗活动相辅相成，我真是喜出望外。随着更频繁地投入非暴力沟通之舞，我更加热爱工作，并深得其乐。”
p62.en: “When I practice medicine, I often use Nonviolent Communication. Some patients asked me if I was a psychologist, because doctors usually did not care about their way of life and their attitude to disease. Nonviolent Communication helps me to be sensitive to their needs and to what they need to hear at certain times. This has been particularly useful in improving relations with patients with haemophilia and people with AIDS, who are often affected by intense anger and suffering. Over the past five years, a woman with AIDS has received my treatment. Recently, she mentioned that I tried to help her find the pleasure of life, which was the best she had. Nonviolent Communication is essential! In the past, once it became known that the patients were suffering from deadly diseases, I was frustrated and had difficulty sincerely encouraging them to embrace life. Through the use of Nonviolent Communication, I have opened my eyes and found new ways of communicating. It is complementary to medical activities, and I am truly impressed. As I engage more frequently in Nonviolent Communication dances, I love and enjoy my work.

p64.original: 还有些人把非暴力沟通运用于政治上。法国的一位内阁成员去看妹妹时，注意到妹妹和妹夫的沟通方式和以前很不一样。听了他们对非暴力沟通的介绍，她深受鼓舞，于是提到下周她需要代表法国，就有关认养程序的一些敏感问题，与阿尔及利亚进行谈判。尽管时间很紧，我们还是请了一位讲法语的培训师去巴黎配合那位内阁部长。后来，她认为，新学习的沟通技巧对谈判的成功有突出的贡献。
p64.en: Others have used Nonviolent Communication for political purposes. When a French cabinet member visited her sister, he noted that her sister and brother-in-law were communicating in different ways than before. She was encouraged to hear their introduction to Nonviolent Communication and noted that she would need to negotiate with Algeria next week on behalf of France on some sensitive issues relating to the adoption process. Despite the time constraints, we have invited a French-speaking trainer to Paris to work with the cabinet minister. Later, she felt that the newly learned communication skills had made a significant contribution to the success of the negotiations.

p65.original: 在耶路撒冷，不同政治立场的以色列人参加了一个非暴力沟通研讨班。参加者使用非暴力沟通对容易引起争议的西岸问题发表他们的意见。许多已在西岸建立家园的以色列人，相信他们的行为是在履行宗教使命。然而，他们所面临的挑战不仅来自巴勒斯坦人，而且来自那些承认这一地区将属于巴勒斯坦的以色列人。其间，我和一位培训师示范了如何以非暴力沟通的方式来倾听，然后请参加者轮流扮演其他人的立场。20分钟后，一位定居者宣布，如果她的政治对手能像刚才那样倾听她的心声，她愿意考虑放弃在西岸的定居点，并迁到国际认可的以色列领土。
p65.en: In Jerusalem, Israelis with different political positions participated in a workshop on Nonviolent Communication. Participants used Nonviolent Communication to express their views on the issues in the West Bank, which were prone to controversy. Many of the Israelis who had established their homes in the West Bank believed that they were acting on religious missions. However, the challenges they face come not only from Palestinians, but also from Israelis who recognize that the area will belong to Palestine. In the meantime, I and a trainer demonstrated how to listen in a non-violent way, and then asked participants to take turns and take the positions of others. Twenty minutes later, a settler announced that if her political opponents could listen to her as they had just done, she would be willing to consider abandoning settlements in the West Bank and moving to internationally recognized Israeli territory.

p66.original: 在世界上，有些地区面临着激烈的暴力冲突以及棘手的种族、宗教或政治问题。非暴力沟通为这些地区提供了有效的解决办法。看到非暴力沟通培训的普及，以及人们使用它来调解以色列、巴勒斯坦、尼日利亚、卢旺达、塞拉利昂以及其他地区的争端，我感到特别地满足。我和工作伙伴曾在贝尔格莱德紧张地工作三天，培训那里为和平工作的市民——他们的国家正在波斯尼亚和克罗地亚进行残酷的战争。我们刚抵达时，学员们看上去十分沮丧。随着培训的进行，我们听到他们咯咯的笑声。他们找到了力量的源泉，并与我们分享他们深深的感激和快乐之情。接下来的两周，我们在克罗地亚、以色列和巴勒斯坦先后开展了培训工作，我们再一次看到，通过运用非暴力沟通，这些处于战乱之中的人们恢复了生活的勇气和信心。
p66.en: In some regions of the world, there are violent and violent conflicts and difficult ethnic, religious or political issues. Nonviolent Communication offers effective solutions in these areas. I am particularly pleased to see the spread of Nonviolent Communication training and its use to mediate disputes in Israel, Palestine, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and elsewhere. I have worked intensively with my working partners for three days in Belgrade to train the citizens who work for peace there — their countries are engaged in brutal wars in Bosnia and Croatia. When we first arrived, the fellows seemed very frustrated. As the training unfolded, we heard them giggle. They found a source of strength and shared with us their deep gratitude and happiness. Over the next two weeks, we have conducted successive training exercises in Croatia, Israel and Palestine, and we have once again seen the courage and confidence of those who are in the midst of war restored through the use of Nonviolent Communication.

p67.original: 0能有机会到世界各地讲解非暴力沟通，体会它所激发的力量和喜悦，我深感幸运。现在，我很高兴，能够通过本书来与你分享非暴力沟通的丰富内容！
p67.en: I am very fortunate to have the opportunity to talk about Nonviolent Communication around the world and to appreciate the power and joy it inspires. Now, I'm happy to be able to share with you the richness of Nonviolent Communication through this book!

p69.original: 非暴力沟通提醒我们专注于彼此的观察、感受、需要和请求。它鼓励倾听，培育尊重与爱，使我们情意相通，乐于互助。有些人用非暴力沟通理解自己，有些人用它改善人际关系，还有人借助它改进工作。在世界各地，非暴力沟通被用来协调各个层面的争论和冲突。
p69.en: Nonviolent Communication reminds us of our focus on each other's observations, feelings, needs and requests. It encourages listening, fosters respect and love, connects us with each other and is happy to help each other. Some understand themselves through Nonviolent Communication, some improve interpersonal relations and others improve their work. Nonviolent Communication has been used throughout the world to reconcile disputes and conflicts at all levels.

p72.original: 本书的许多章节带有题为“非暴力沟通在行动”的对话。这些对话是想请读者体会非暴力沟通原则的实际应用。然而，非暴力沟通不只是语言表达或使用文字的技巧，它所包含的意识和意图，也可以通过沉默、专注以及面部表情和身体语言来表达。你将读到的“非暴力沟通在行动”的对话，是实际对话的摘要和删节版。在实际的对话中，静静的倾听、故事、幽默、姿势等，使双方的交流比书中浓缩之后的对话显得自然。
p72.en: Many chapters of the book contain a dialogue entitled “Nonviolent Communication in action”. These dialogues are intended to draw readers ' attention to the practical application of the principle of Nonviolent Communication. However, Nonviolent Communication is not just a technique of speech or use of words, but also includes a sense of consciousness and intent that can be expressed through silence, focus, and facial and physical expressions. The dialogue that you will read “Nonviolent Communication in action” is a summary and abridged version of the actual dialogue. In the actual dialogue, silence, stories, humor, pose etc. makes it natural that the two sides communicate more than the dialogue that has been condensed in the book.

p73.original: 我曾在伯利恒德黑萨难民营中的一个清真寺讲解非暴力沟通。听众是巴勒斯坦的穆斯林男子，大约有170人。那时，巴勒斯坦人对美国人的态度并不友好。演说的时候，我突然注意到，听众中传来一阵低沉的声音。我的翻译提醒我：“他们正低声议论你是美国人！”此时，一位男子站了起来。他冲着我使劲喊道：“谋杀犯！”许多人立即随声附和，大喊：“杀手！”“杀孩子的凶手！”“谋杀犯！”
p73.en: I spoke about Nonviolent Communication in a mosque in the Dar-Hesse refugee camp in Bethlehem. The audience is composed of approximately 170 Muslim men from Palestine. At that time, the attitude of Palestinians towards the Americans was not friendly. When I spoke, I suddenly noticed that there was a low voice in the audience. My interpreter reminds me, "They're whispering about you as an American." At this point, a man stood up. He shouted at me, "Survivors! Many people immediately joined the peace and shouted, "Skiller! "The Killer of the Child! "The Murderer!

p74.original: 十分幸运的是，我能够全神贯注地体会那个男人当时的感受和需要。我对这种情况的发生早有预感。来难民营的路上，我看到几个前一天晚上射入难民营的催泪弹弹壳。每个弹壳上，“美国制造”这几个字都十分醒目。我知道，对于美国供应催泪弹和其他武器给以色列，这些难民心中充满愤怒。
p74.en: Fortunately, I was able to see the man's feelings and needs with all my attention. I had a feeling that that was happening. On the way to the camp, I saw several tear gas shells that had been fired into the camp the previous night. The words “made in the United States” are very sharp on every shell shell. I know that these refugees are filled with anger at the United States supply of tear gas and other weapons to Israel.

p75.original: 我和那个称我为谋杀犯的男人开始对话：
p75.en: I started talking to the man who called me a murderer:

p77.original: 我：“你生气是因为你想要我的政府改变它使用资源的方式吗？”（我不知道我猜得对不对，但关键是，我确实关心他的感受和需要。）
p77.en: I said, "Are you angry because you want my government to change the way it uses its resources? ”I don't know if I guess right, but the point is that I really care about his feelings and needs. I don't think so.

p78.original: 他：“天杀的，我当然生气！你以为我们需要催泪弹？我们需要的是排水管，不是你们的催泪弹！我们需要的是房子！我们需要建立自己的国家！”
p78.en: And he said, "God damn it, I'm angry! You think we need tear gas? What we need is a drain pipe, not your tear gas! What we need is a house! We need to build our own country!

p79.original: 我：“所以，你很愤怒，你想要一些支持来改善生活条件并在政治上独立？”
p79.en: I said, “So, you're angry and you want some support to improve living conditions and political independence?

p80.original: 他：“你知道我们带着小孩在这里住27年是什么感觉吗？你对我们长期以来的生活状况有一点点认识吗？”
p80.en: He said, "Do you know what it's like for us to live here with our kids for 27 years? Do you know a little bit about our long-standing life?

p81.original: 我：“听起来，你感到绝望。你想知道，我或别人是不是能够真正了解这种生活的滋味？”
p81.en: I said, "You sound desperate. Do you want to know if I or anyone else can really understand the taste of this life?

p82.original: 他：“你想了解吗？告诉我，你有孩子吗？他们上学吗？他们有运动场吗？我儿子病了！他在水沟里玩耍！他的教室里没有书！你见过没有书的学校吗？”
p82.en: He said, "Do you want to understand? Tell me, do you have children? Are they going to school? Do they have a stadium? My son is sick! He's playing in the ditch! There's no book in his classroom! Have you ever seen a school without a book?

p83.original: 我：“我注意到，你在这里培养孩子，是多么地痛苦！你想告诉我，你所要的正是所有父母想给孩子的——好的教育，以及健康的环境来让他们玩耍和成长……”
p83.en: I said, "I noticed how painful it is to be here to raise a child! You want to tell me that what all parents want is a good education and a healthy environment for their children to play and grow...”

p84.original: 他：“不错，这些是最基本的。人权——你们美国人不是说这是人权吗？何不让更多的美国人来这里看看你们给这里带来了什么样的人权！”
p84.en: And he said, "That's good. These are the basics. Human rights - Don't you Americans say it's human rights? Why don't more Americans come here and see what kind of human rights you've brought here?

p85.original: 我：“你是希望更多的美国人了解你们巨大的痛苦，并意识到我们政治活动的后果吗？”
p85.en: I said, “Do you want more Americans to understand your great suffering and realize the consequences of our political activities?

p87.original: 我们的对话持续了将近二十分钟，他一直在表达痛苦，而我倾听每句话所包含的情感和需要。他主动帮助我了解他的心灵以及深深的不幸。我并不将他的话视为攻击，而当作来自人类同胞的礼物。
p87.en: Our dialogue lasted almost 20 minutes, and he has been expressing his pain, and I have listened to the emotions and needs contained in every sentence. He took the initiative to help me understand his heart and his deep sorrow. I do not regard his words as an attack, but as a gift from fellow human beings.

p88.original: 当这位先生感到我领会了他的意思，他开始愿意听我讲我来难民营的目的。一个小时后，这个原来称我为谋杀犯的男子邀请我去他家享用丰盛的斋月晚餐。
p88.en: When the gentleman felt that I understood his intentions, he began to listen to me about the purpose of my presence in the camp. An hour later, the man who originally called me a murderer invited me to his house for a good Ramadan dinner.
